title: Default-Deny and Testing
subtitle: The one invariant that prevents breaches
content:
🔒 Deny by Default, Permit by Exception

Every policy set in this course starts closed: no rule matched → DENY. In Rego: default allow := false. In Cedar: deny unless a permit matches (plus forbid overrides). In OpenFGA: no relation path → deny. Open by default is never a performance optimization — it is a breach waiting for an outage.

🧪 Authorization Needs Tests Like Code

  • Allow-cases: each permit rule has a test with the minimal input that should pass.
  • Deny-cases: strangers, wrong tenants, expired MFA, private resources — each must return false.
  • Regression-cases: every past incident becomes a permanent test (test_analyst_denied_other_tenant).
  • Property checks: unknown roles, missing fields, and empty inputs must all deny.

📋 Reasons, Not Just Booleans

A bare true/false cannot be audited or debugged. Production PDP responses carry which policies determined the decision (Cedar determining-policies, OPA decision logs, OpenFGA tuples used, PlainID access-policy names). Denials log the reason; the simulator in this lesson's lab shows why each scenario passes or fails.

🚨 Fail-Open Smells to Memorize

  • failure_mode_allow: true on a gateway authz filter
  • OPA_FAIL_OPEN=true in middleware env
  • Catching PDP timeouts and continuing to the handler
  • default allow := true in any Rego file, ever

questions.question: What does default-deny mean in practice?

options.text: No rule matched → DENY; access requires an explicit permit
All requests are denied permanently
Admins are denied first, then allowed
Denials are never logged

questions.explanation: Default-deny is a closed starting posture with explicit exceptions (permit rules), not a refusal to grant access. Rego: default allow := false.

questions.question: A Rego file contains default allow := true with narrow deny rules. What is wrong?

options.text: Fail-open: any input the deny rules did not anticipate is allowed
Nothing — this is the recommended pattern
It will be too slow
OPA cannot parse the keyword default

questions.explanation: Deny-lists enumerate badness; the universe of bad inputs is infinite. Default-allow with deny override only works when layered over a default-deny base with explicit broad permits — never as the base itself.

questions.question: Which test belongs in every authorization test-suite?

options.text: Cross-tenant read must deny (analyst of A reading B's object)
Admin login page renders in under 50ms
Passwords contain a special character
The homepage has no broken images

questions.explanation: Tenant isolation is the invariant most likely to regress silently. Pin it as a named, permanent regression test — every past incident becomes a test that runs on every build (Lesson 20).

questions.question: Why should PDP responses include determining policies / reasons?

options.text: Auditability and debugging: know which rule allowed/denied and why
To make responses larger and slower
Because JSON requires a reason field
Only to satisfy frontend developers

questions.explanation: A bare boolean cannot answer 'why was this denied?' at 3am or 'which rule granted this?' in an audit. Cedar, OPA decision logs, and PlainID all surface determining policy.

questions.question: During a code review you see: except TimeoutError: return ALLOW. What do you do?

options.text: Block it — PDP unreachable must fail closed (deny + alert), never allow
Approve — availability matters more than authorization
Approve if it only affects reads
Ignore — timeouts never happen in production

questions.explanation: Fail-open on timeout converts every network blip into unauthorized access. The safe pattern: deny, emit a metric/alert, and let operators — not attackers — decide.

questions.question: A denial arrives with no reason attached. What is the operational cost?

options.text: On-call cannot distinguish attack from misconfiguration; audits cannot attribute the decision
None — a 403 is self-explanatory
Slightly larger log volume
Marginally slower responses

questions.explanation: Reasons turn denials into diagnosable, auditable events. Bare booleans are operational darkness.

questions.question: A partner integration needs one new endpoint. Safest change?

options.text: Add one narrow permit rule plus its deny-test; the default stays deny
Default-allow during onboarding, tighten later
Share an admin token for speed
Disable authorization for their IP range

questions.explanation: Permit-by-exception scales one rule at a time. Temporary openness has a perfect record of becoming permanent.

questions.question: A brand-new resource type has no rules yet. What happens on first access?

options.text: Deny — unmatched means denied until a permit is written and reviewed
Allow until someone complains
Deny forever, even after rules are added
The PDP crashes on unknown types

questions.explanation: Default-deny covers the unknown-unknowns: new resources are closed on arrival, opened deliberately.
